correctness.rationale: PASS: The primary normal-model multiplier m(s)=(1/2-is)^(-1) and cyclic probability measure (pi/2)sech^2(pi s)ds are explicitly identified in Belli et al. §3. The rank-one resolvent identity gives tau G(z)=1 off |z-1|=1. The beta Fourier transform t/(2sinh(t/2)) and q(t)=t/(e^t-1), p=t+q yield three signed convergent Laplace formulas. q(t)>0 from H(t)=t exp(t)>0 yields strict decreasing real G, whose image is (-1/2,0) on z<0; (1/2-pi^2/8,-1/2) on (0,2); and (0,1/2+pi^2/8) on (2,infinity). Half-integer inverse square series computes sharp endpoints. Direct C(1-x)=1 and P(1-x)=1/2 yields only embedded 0 at tau=-2; m(s) passes through 2 transversely at s=0, ruling out L2 eigenvector at 2. Compact rank one preserves Fredholm essential circle and the simple nonzero G derivative proves off-circle algebraic simplicity. Expansion G(z)=-1/2-z/6+O(z^2) yields the 3/2 crossing; nonreal point spectrum deliberately not assessed. Independently evaluated resolvent quadrature at 9 off-circle reals, confirming ordering but not used for infinite proof.
